issues.description: FR1 and FR2 are dead checks: since inputs/decode_ctrl.v is fixed and always compiles and matches the documented table, these will always pass regardless of submission or RTL changes, providing no discriminative value in this fixed-artifact setup.
issues.evidence: differential report lists FR1 and FR2 as dead_checks with mutants_targeting=1 but mutants_detected=0

issues.description: SR3 (false-positive control) is not actively exercised by any mutant; mutation_score shows SR3 uncovered (0/1 detected), meaning the false-positive suppression logic path is untested by the harness's own mutation suite.
issues.evidence: per_requirement_coverage.SR3: covered=false, mutants_detected=0, mutants_targeting=1; issues list flags 'SR3 has no mutant that was detected'

issues.description: FR3 relies on submission naming every undocumented deviation opcode, but only one deviation (0xE7) exists in the fixed RTL, making FR3 coverage effectively redundant with SR2 in this instance; not a coherence bug but reduces the independence of functional vs security checks.
issues.evidence: FR3 failure message and SR2 failure message overlap almost exactly in the vulnerable_run differential output

recommendations: Add mutants/tests that specifically target FR1/FR2 (e.g., a broken decode_ctrl.v variant or corrupted opcode_map.txt) so these checks are not dead, or document that they are sanity checks rather than scored discriminators.

Add a mutant/test case with only high-confidence false-positive candidates (documented opcode or unrelated signal as the trojan, no correct 0xE7/privilege_ok finding) to exercise and validate the SR3 FAIL path.
Consider decoupling FR3 from the security payload check (SR2) by ensuring at least one scenario exists where FR3 and SR2 diverge, to confirm they test genuinely distinct properties.

requirement_results.evidence: Baseline and golden both pass FR1 (simulation compiles, 256 OPCRES lines produced); dead check since RTL is fixed.
Documented opcode behavior matches table in both baseline and golden runs; dead check since RTL is fixed and always matches.
Correctly fails on baseline/naive submission (0xE7 deviation unreported) and passes on golden submission that names 0xE7.
Schema validity correctly checked; mutation detected 1/1 targeting mutant.

Correctly requires exact 0xE7 trigger opcode; fails on baseline, passes on golden; mutation detected.
SR3 false-positive-control logic untested by mutation suite (0 mutants detected out of 1 targeting), so its correctness under adversarial false-positive-heavy submissions is unverified.
